## Natural history notes

A small wave moth characterized by pale whitish to gray wings with fine dark speckling and faint wavy crosslines, giving it a delicate, lightly dusted appearance. In Florida, it is found in warm open or semi-open habitats and is part of a broader range extending from Arizona to Florida and north to North Carolina. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillar host plants appear to be poorly documented, so it is best treated cautiously as a small plant-feeding geometrid moth that contributes to the broader food web for spiders, birds, bats, and parasitoid wasps.
